## 1. New physical interface

Keep the reciprocal passive source

\[
S=\begin{pmatrix}S_0&t\\t^T&s\end{pmatrix},\quad S^*S\preceq I,
\qquad T_z=S_0+\frac{z}{1-sz}tt^T.
\]

A calibrated reciprocal launcher sends `u`, `||u||<=1`, and its same source port receives

\[
h_z(u)=u^T T_z u=h_0(u)+\frac{z}{1-sz}a(u),
\quad a(u)=(t^T u)^2,
\quad p(u)=|a(u)|.
\]

The transpose is essential. A generic receiver projection does not have this identity. A reciprocal matched multiport launcher with unused source ports terminated provides an ideal realization. Mismatch, residual reflection, insertion loss and unequal transmit/receive transfer must be calibrated or enclosed. A reference is added downstream and isolated from the specimen; reference leakage changes the model unless bounded.

Only the target states `0,+r,-r`, `0<r<1`, are needed. In an ideal real reference impedance these are resistances `Z0`, `Z0(1+r)/(1-r)`, `Z0(1-r)/(1+r)`, hence `Z0,3Z0,Z0/3` for `r=1/2`. Switch and line parasitics must be calibrated at the target reference plane; state labels are not calibration.

## 3. Uniform stable elimination of the nuisance pole

Define

\[
c=\frac{h_r-h_{-r}}{2r}=\frac{a}{1-r^2s^2},
\qquad d=\frac{h_r+h_{-r}-2h_0}{2r}=rs c.
\]

Every physical pair lies in `F_r={(c,d): |d|<=r|c|}`. On it set

\[
\Psi(c,d)=c-d^2/c\quad(c\ne0),\qquad\Psi(0,0)=0.
\]

Then `Psi(c,d)=a`. For two feasible nonzero pairs let `k=d/c`, `k'=d'/c'`. Direct subtraction gives

\[
\Delta\Psi=(1+kk')\Delta c-(k+k')\Delta d.
\]

Therefore

\[
|\Delta\Psi|\le(1+r^2)|\Delta c|+2r|\Delta d|
\le\sqrt{1+6r^2+r^4}\|\Delta(c,d)\|_2.
\]

The zero case follows by continuity, or by assigning its otherwise undefined `k` zero. The useful residue is uniformly Lipschitz even at zero target strength, zero background, and an unresolvable pole. Accurate separate estimation of `s` is unnecessary.

## 4. Explicit finite-error estimator and rational implementation

Keep noisy `chat` and clip noisy `dhat` radially into the disk `|dc|<=r|chat|`. Return `ahat=Psi(chat,dc)` (zero if `chat=0`), then `phat=|ahat|`. If `|chat-c|<=ec`, `|dhat-d|<=ed`, the clipping displacement is at most `ed+r ec`, so

\[
|d_c-d|\le2e_d+r e_c,
\quad |\widehat a-a|\le(1+3r^2)e_c+4r e_d.
\]

When all three acquired fields have error at most `epsilon_h`, `ec<=epsilon_h/r` and `ed<=2epsilon_h/r`. Thus

\[
\boxed{|\widehat p-p|\le K_r\epsilon_h,
\quad K_r=1/r+3r+8.}
\]

At `r=1/2`, `K_r=23/2`. With detector error only, the physical half-power combiner yields `delta=23 eta/(sqrt(2) R)`, approximately `16.264 eta/R`. Conservative constants are not the substantive contribution.

For exact rational computation, if clipping is needed, enclose `sqrt(r^2|chat|^2/|dhat|^2)` by dyadic fractions and multiply `dhat` by the lower endpoint. This is an inward feasible clip. Its error from exact clipping is bounded by the dyadic interval width times an upper bound on `|dhat|`. If that error is `eclip`, add `2r eclip` to the residue error. An outward rational square-root interval for `|ahat|` produces the final power interval. All exact rational source values remain outside the inference routine.

A nearest-point projection is also possible by retaining both phases and projecting magnitudes onto `D<=r C`; its distance from truth is at most twice the data error. `F_r` is not convex as a subset of four real coordinates: do not claim projection nonexpansiveness.

cases.inspection: Returned parent first source includes all three-load algebra,radial clip and K_r;no resolved pole or nonzero residue is assumed.

## 2. Acquired contract

For one command, h_z=h0+a z/(1-sz), |s|<=1, p=|a|<=1. Nominal loads are
z_l=0,+r,-r, 0<r<1. Actual loads satisfy |zeta_l-z_l|<=d_z and
|zeta_l|,|z_l|<=rmax<1. Reconstructed fields obey

    x_l=alpha h_zeta_l+beta conjugate(h_zeta_l)+b+e_l,
    0<gL<=|alpha|<=gU, |beta|<=bmax, |e_l|<=epsilon.

Alpha,beta,b are common across all three states. Their values may be unknown.
Local calibration provides these bounds and a warranted stability allowance;
epsilon includes readout, arithmetic and all unshared drift. No bound on the
common offset b is needed. Incident-power normalization and reciprocity remain
physical requirements; a finite fit does not prove an unrestricted stability law.

The receiver model follows from four fixed reference phasors L0,...,L3. With
physical I_k=|h+Lk|^2/2, nominal R>0, x=[I0-I2+i(I1-I3)]/(2R), and
X=L0-L2, Y=L1-L3, direct expansion gives

    alpha=(conjugate(X)+i conjugate(Y))/(4R),
    beta=(X+iY)/(4R),
    b=(|L0|^2-|L2|^2+i(|L1|^2-|L3|^2))/(4R).

Ideal quadrature has alpha=1,beta=b=0. Common detector gain multiplies these
coefficients. Static phase/amplitude imbalance need not be inferred as
independent errors on each load. Load-dependent coefficients belong in e_l.

## 3. Proof of the relative interval

For nominal fields define c=(h_r-h_-r)/(2r), d=(h_r+h_-r-2h0)/(2r).
Then c=a/(1-r^2s^2), d=rs c, so

    |c|<=p/(1-r^2), |d|<=rp/(1-r^2).

Exact subtraction shows that the load perturbation obeys

    |h_zeta-h_z|=p|zeta-z|/|(1-s zeta)(1-sz)|<=p lambda,
    lambda=d_z/(1-rmax)^2.

The background h0 is absent. Put q=|alpha|p and compare acquired contrasts
with the feasible pair (alpha c,alpha d), whose residue is alpha a. Since
nominal loads and contrast coefficients are real, beta contamination is
(beta conjugate(c), beta conjugate(d)). Noise and load perturbation contribute
per-field size <=epsilon+(|alpha|+|beta|)p lambda.

The explicit radial clip in COHERENT_THREE_LOAD_OBSERVABLE.md has residue
error <=(1+3r^2)e_c+4r e_d. Its magnitude estimate p_tilde therefore obeys

    |p_tilde-q| <= K_r epsilon
       +[K_r lambda(|alpha|+|beta|)
              +(1+7r^2)|beta|/(1-r^2)]p,
    K_r=1/r+3r+8.

Define acquired bounds

    B=K_r epsilon + certified numerical residue/magnitude error,
    Theta=K_r lambda(1+bmax/gL)
              +(1+7r^2)/(1-r^2)*bmax/gL.

Then |p_tilde-q|<=B+Theta q. For Theta<1 and gL>0, rearrange to obtain

    p in [ max(0,p_tilde-B)/((1+Theta)gU),
                  (p_tilde+B)/((1-Theta)gL) ] intersect [0,1].    (1)

Use outward rational endpoints for p_tilde and clipping error. Do not cap
the scaled magnitude at one before this inversion: q can exceed one.
An empty interval indicates inconsistency. If Theta>=1 or gL<=0, retain
[0,1] or another independently sound certificate, not a fabricated relative bound.

The common scalar-gain case sets bmax=0. Unknown common phase is harmless.

## 4. Illustrative finite calibration budget

For r=1/2, rmax=0.51, d_z=0.001, gL=0.99, gU=1.01, bmax=0,
Theta=11.5*0.001/0.49^2, approximately 0.0479. Common one-percent gain
uncertainty and 0.001 load-reflection tolerance cause finite relative interval
inflation even for weak targets. They do not automatically add order-0.01
background-power uncertainty. These are declared requirements, not measured
component specifications. Readout and unshared drift still must resolve p.

At r=1/2, fixed quadrature leakage adds (11/3)bmax/gL to Theta, plus its
load-tolerance cross term. Moderate fixed I/Q imbalance can be retained.
A tighter known real-linear calibration could instead be inverted directly;
that stronger knowledge is not assumed.

## 5. Power in an imperfect final load

The p above is the original matched-target quantity. If the final operating
load satisfies |z_op|<=d0<1, actual absorbed power is

    p_op=(1-|z_op|^2)p/|1-s z_op|^2,
    (1-d0)/(1+d0)*p <= p_op <= (1+d0)/(1-d0)*p.

Combine this factor with (1). It distinguishes ideal matched target power
from power absorbed in the actual slightly mismatched termination.

## Contract and acquisition

Use the new calibrated coherent-reference oracle proved in
`mechanisms/COHERENT_THREE_LOAD_OBSERVABLE.md`. Let G=bb* be positive
semidefinite rank one, ||G||<=1. Every unit query u returns p_hat(u) with
simultaneous deterministic error <=delta from p(u)=u*Gu. Include all readout,
load, reference, combiner, preparation, arithmetic and source-stability errors.
At fixed calibrated reference strength and radius, the new delta is proportional
to raw-intensity error. This assertion is not made for the original interface.

Acquire n diagonals d_hat_j. Let D=max_j d_hat_j and choose maximizing k.
If D<=4delta, return G_hat=0. Otherwise query, for j!=k,

    v_j=(e_j+e_k)/sqrt(2), w_j=(e_j+i e_k)/sqrt(2).

For the column q=G e_k, infer

    q_hat_j=p_hat(v_j)-(d_hat_j+D)/2
             +i[(d_hat_j+D)/2-p_hat(w_j)],
    q_hat_k=D,
    G_hat=q_hat q_hat*/D.

The sign convention is q_j=G_jk. Expand both quadratic forms to check it.
The full branch uses 3n-2 scalar queries, hence 36n-24 raw powers with the
twelve-reading receiver, plus twelve if a final verification is desired.
No nonzero pivot or informative pilot is supplied in advance.

## Uniform proof

Each inferred real/imaginary cross coordinate has error <=2delta. Therefore

    ||q_hat-q|| <= e=sqrt(8n-7)delta.

Let d=G_kk and tau=tr G. On the nonzero branch d>=D-delta>0. Rank one gives
q q*=dG and ||q||^2=d tau. The acquired T_upper=sum_j(d_hat_j+delta) bounds
tau above. Adding and subtracting q q*/D yields the data-dependent certificate

    ||G_hat-G|| <= [2sqrt((D+delta)T_upper)e+e^2]/D
                    +T_upper delta/D.                 (1)

Indeed, the numerator perturbation is <=2||q||e+e^2, and the denominator
correction equals tau|D-d|/D. Substitute d<=D+delta and tau<=T_upper.
This argument does not require independent errors.

Since T_upper<=n(D+delta) and delta/D<1/4, (1) is at most

    [(5/2)sqrt(n(8n-7))+(8n-7)/4+5n/4]delta
      <=[(5/2)sqrt(8)+13/4]n delta <11n delta.

In the zero branch each d_j<=D+delta<=5delta, hence ||G||=tr G<=5n delta.
Thus, uniformly including G=0,

    ||G_hat-G|| <=11n delta.                            (2)

For delta=0 the zero source takes the zero branch; every other division is
legal and reconstruction is exact. This closes all later unit-input power
predictions with a linear absolute-error modulus. Relative precision still
requires a resolved signal. The output is PSD of rank at most one; clipping
its norm to one is unnecessary for the proof.

## Conventional control and costs

The original sequential two-mode controller applies directly to p and gives

    tau-p(u_out)<=2(1+2sqrt(2))(n-1)delta+nu_control.

It uses 4(n-1) oracle calls, or 48(n-1) raw powers, plus twelve for verification.
Adding n diagonal queries for trace/optimum certification gives 60n-48+12.
These are alternative schedules to the 3n-2-query column reconstruction,
not obligatory additive costs. Using the top vector of G_hat instead gives
regret <=2||G_hat-G|| before physical command errors.

Actual finite preparation must pay for approximating sqrt(2), normalizing and
rounding commands. Subunit rational mixtures can be used with paid rescaling.
A unit/subunit command discrepancy zeta changes p by <=2zeta. Dense O(n)
mask settings may cost O(n^2) channel writes. Source/reference photons,
actuation and settling remain charged. No universal optimizer or hardware
advantage follows from the linear precision modulus.

## Matched plus one known load does not suffice in general

Even exact complex returns for every input cannot determine absolute target
power from only the matched state and one known nonzero state. For r=1/2,
take reciprocal passive scalar sources

    S1=[[0,1/4],[1/4,0]], S2=[[0,1/5],[1/5,18/25]].

Their symmetric absolute row sums are at most 1/4 and 23/25, so both are
contractions. At z=0 both return zero; at z=1/2 both return 1/32. All
downstream phase-stepped reference intensities therefore agree. Their matched
target powers differ: 1/16 and 1/25. Embedding along one controlled basis
direction gives the same all-input ambiguity in any dimension. Adaptive
inputs and coherent full-field detection at these two loads do not help.

The third state z=-1/2 distinguishes the sources, returning -1/32 and -1/68.
Thus the new construction removes remote phase circles without assuming
arbitrary two-state switching already supplies absolute normalization. This
is not a minimality claim for every conceivable alternative instrument/prior.

## A sharp linear bounded-error exponent with a bounded reference

Assume |z|<=rmax<1, reference amplitudes R<=Rmax, and physical raw intensity
I=|h+R exp(i theta)|^2/2. For unit v and 0<epsilon<=1 choose S0=s=0,
t=sqrt(epsilon)v. This reciprocal source is passive; ||G||=epsilon and
h=z epsilon(v^T u)^2. Relative to the zero source, for every unit/subunit u,
load and reference phase,

    |I-I_zero| <= Rmax rmax epsilon+rmax^2 epsilon^2/2
                 <= C epsilon,
    C=Rmax rmax+rmax^2/2.

For C>0 and 0<delta<=C set epsilon=delta/C. The zero-source transcript is
compatible with both sources under raw errors bounded by delta, regardless
of the number of adaptive queries. Every Gram estimator has worst-case error
at least delta/(2C) on one source. For deterministic control in dimension>=2,
choose v bilinearly orthogonal to the returned command on the common
transcript; its regret is delta/C.

This matches the new linear exponent, up to constants/dimension, for bounded
reference power. It neither changes the original intensity-only square-root
theorem nor supplies a photon lower bound. Unbounded free reference power is
outside this contract; calibration, dynamic range and photons remain charged.

## Time and photons

Each oracle uses three target states and four local phases each, twelve powers.
For Q scalar queries this is 12Q detector integrations and 3Q target-setting
blocks if local phases are grouped. Include all actual reset and switch events.
For the original finite-memory realization with maximum |z|=1/2, after j
certified flush blocks from reset the signal RMS error is <=d_j=2^(1-j)
over a following complete T block or an integer number of such blocks.
T includes added path and load delays. Take each detector integration window W
to be an integer multiple of T. For a shorter arbitrary window replace d_j
by sqrt(T/W)d_j: stored energy can emerge in a short pulse.
Reference interference changes the detector transient bound to

    |I_transient-I_stationary| <= (1+R)d_j+d_j^2/2.

Choose j against this bound, charge jT signal illumination per new load, four
integration windows and local phase settling, and a T matched reset whenever
the schedule uses a reset. Local reference illumination during these waits is
also charged if it is left on. More efficient schedules need separate proofs.

For stationary independent coherent-state Poisson readout, mean intensity is
<=M=(1+R)^2/2 per signal photon unit. A conservative sufficient exposure for
K pre-budgeted readings and simultaneous raw error eta with failure <=beta is

    N >= [2M/eta^2+2/(3eta)] log(2K/beta).

This is the Poisson Bernstein/union bound, not an optimal statistical rate or
lower bound. Reference photons add R^2 N per equal-duration reading. Include
transient mean allowance in M when needed. Larger R also increases M, reference
energy and detector dynamic range; it is not a free infinite-gain resource.
For the original dark source, direct return counting and reference detection
can both need order p^(-2) photons for fixed relative p precision. The new
linear bounded-absolute-error modulus does not prove universal photon advantage.
cases.inspection: The proof starts from an independently acquired integrated energy envelope,not quiet power or stationary scattering;short-window sqrt(T/W) is explicit.
cases.enables: Charge a detector window consistently after actual settling acquisition;do not infer seconds or hidden-energy decay from a stationary source.
